children: Basis bids for corn shipped by barge to US Gulf Coast export terminals were flat to weaker on Wednesday. Basis bids for soybeans were unchanged.
CIF corn barges loaded in December were bid at 95 cents a bushel over Chicago Board of Trade December futures
, falling 2 cents. They were offered at 97 cents over futures, falling 3 cents.
CIF corn barges loaded in December traded at 97 and 98 cents over CBOT December corn
CIF soybean barges loaded in January traded at 114 cents a bushel over CBOT January futures
South Korean importer Cargill Agri Purina (CAPI) purchased up to 67,000 metric tons of animal feed corn to be sourced from South America or South Africa only in an international tender on Tuesday.
Crops from the recent US Midwest harvest continued to flow into supply chains.
Ahead of Thursday's weekly USDA export sales report, analysts expected the government to report US soybean sales in the week ended November 12 at 1,000,000-2,000,000 metric tons.
Analysts expected weekly corn sales at 1,200,000-2,000,000 tons.
CBOT December corn ended down 11-1/4 cents, or 2.52%, at $4.35-1/2 a bushel.
finished down 8-3/4 cents, or 0.71%, at $12.16-3/4 a bushel.
